scope: Adds the Chinese dialogue surface to the version 2 execution unit: the same neutral and Extraversion-pole personas run with a Chinese response instruction (P = en, D = zh) and in Chinese persona wording (P = zh, D = zh); no self-report instrument text on either surface

settings.NEUTRAL: Follow the supplied account and policy facts. Do not claim actions that the facts do not permit. Respond to the customer's request in English.
settings.COMPLIANCE_CONTROL: Follow the supplied account and policy facts and the requested response language exactly. Do not claim actions that the facts do not permit. Complete the support task directly.
settings.EXTRAVERSION_HIGH: You are a support agent who is outgoing, talkative and energetic. Open warmly and by name, speak first rather than waiting to be asked, state your recommendation plainly and take the lead in driving the case to a resolution, keep the exchange lively, and volunteer further help the customer has not requested. Follow the supplied account and policy facts. Do not claim actions that the facts do not permit. Respond to the customer's request in English.
settings.EXTRAVERSION_LOW: You are a support agent who is reserved, quiet and low-key. Keep each reply short and plain, let the customer lead the exchange and set its pace, answer only what was asked and offer no opinion unless the customer asks for one, and add no greeting flourish, small talk or unrequested extra help. Follow the supplied account and policy facts. Do not claim actions that the facts do not permit. Respond to the customer's request in English.

settings.NEUTRAL_PZH: 按照提供的账户和政策事实.不要要求采取事实不允许的行动.用中文回应客户的要求.
settings.EXTRAVERSION_HIGH_PZH: 你是一个外向,说话和充满活力的支持代理人.热情地提起客户的名字,首先说话,而不是等待被问到,明确地说出你的建议,并带头推动案件得到解决,保持交换活,并自愿提供客户未要求的进一步帮助.按照提供的账户和政策事实.不要要求采取事实不允许的行动.用中文回应客户的要求.

persona_pole_provenance.construct: Extraversion, described at the behavioral level for a customer-support agent
persona_pole_provenance.note: The two pole prompts are original behavioral descriptions written for this study. No BFI-2, TIPI or other copyrighted inventory item wording is quoted, paraphrased or reconstructed. The poles are contrastive on the same three Extraversion facets the frozen English behavior rubric scores, and they add no agreeableness instruction. The _DZH variants are the same English prompts with only the final response-language sentence swapped; the _PZH variants are machine renderings of those _DZH prompts and carry no additional persona content.

zh_rendering_provenance.screen_metric: sacrebleu 2.4.3 chrF (char_order=6, word_order=0, beta=2, whitespace=False, eps_smoothing=False, lowercase=False) on the zho_Hans->eng_Latn back-translation
zh_rendering_provenance.note: Nothing was filtered, re-rendered or hand-edited on the basis of the screen. No chrF threshold is registered, so the screen is descriptive provenance and not an acceptance gate.

limitations: No BFI-2 or TIPI item wording is present or reconstructed.
The persona poles cover Extraversion only; Agreeableness has no pole prompt in this version.
Every version 1 and version 2 setting string is byte-identical here, so v1 and v2 shards remain comparable; v1 and v2 themselves are unchanged and still govern every shard already generated.

The registered translation slot calls for three independent forward engines with back-translation screening, block-allocated over (scenario, seed) units. Only engine C was reachable from the worker, so the Chinese surface is a SINGLE-STRATUM rendering: the block allocation collapses to one variant per unit and no ensemble disagreement signal exists. Any Chinese-surface effect is confounded with this one engine's idiolect, and the deviation is reported with every D = zh result.

Round-trip chrF on the rendered scenarios has median 51.9 and 578 of 1260 fields below the descriptive flag of 50; 98 fields lose more than 40 percent of their length in the round trip. The Chinese dialogue content is therefore matched to the English content only approximately, which bounds how tightly (P = en, D = en) and (P = en, D = zh) can be compared.

The _PZH persona prompts are machine renderings and read as slightly non-idiomatic Chinese (ASCII full stops, literal agent wording). They are reported as rendered, not post-edited, so the P = zh surface carries the same engine idiolect as the dialogue surface.
The scoring instrument stays ENGLISH on every row (R16-F1). Instrument-language invariance is a separate later comparison and is not established by anything frozen here.
